# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 62 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 62 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_062_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 62 develops the flesh-spirit anthropology further. Three categories emerge: (1) those who kept spirit and flesh pure — they receive eternal life; (2) those who kept the commandment (spirit) but defiled the flesh — they live, but with a shortened life; (3) those who departed from God and did not repent — they die.

The definition of "defiling the flesh" as "departing from God" (*apochorein apo tou theou*) is Hermas's characteristic move: moral purity is primarily relational (with God) rather than ritual. The double-minded are the primary mechanism of this departure.

The phrase "those who have been called by the name of God" (*hoi onomazomenoi*) is a technical term for Christians — those who bear the Name.

"Deprived themselves of God's salvation" (*esterēsan heautous tēs zōēs*) — the reflexive *heautous* is important: Hermas insists that self-exclusion from salvation is the structure of damnation. God does not actively condemn; people deprive themselves.

---

## Similitude 5, Part 8 — On Defiling the Flesh

**62:1** I asked him to explain why the flesh is destroyed when the soul is saved. "Listen," he said. "Those who have kept their spirit pure from the beginning and have not defiled it — these are righteous. The Lord sees and approves their spirit and grants them eternal life."

**62:2** "But those who have kept the commandment of God but have not kept their flesh, and have defiled it — these also shall live, but the life they shall live will be somewhat shorter. As one who knows the Lord's commandment but does not keep it incurs his own loss."

**62:3** "Lord," I said, "I do not yet understand. What is this defilement of the flesh?" "Listen," he said. "To depart from God is to defile the flesh. Any person who associates with the deeds of the double-minded departs from God and defiles himself."

**62:4** "But those who live in forgetfulness and deceive themselves with their so-called knowledge — these also shall live, but not as those who have kept the commandment purely. For those who have departed from God, sinned, and not repented shall die. And those who go away sorrowfully are those who sinned and repented; on that account they live, but their life is shortened."

**62:5** When I had heard these things and understood them well, I said: "Lord, what exactly do you mean by all this?" He said to me: "I am speaking about those who have been called by the name of God, and have gone astray through love of possessions and wealth and power and the vanity of this world. These are the ones who have deprived themselves of God's salvation."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
